description: Run increasing decode lengths to find the crossover point where B011 residency cache becomes faster than B010 repeated acquisition. This tests the amortization hypothesis empirically rather than assuming it.
experimental_question: At what workload size does residency become faster than repeated acquisition?

telemetry_refinements.cache_population_cost: Separate first-pass copy time from steady-state residency cost
telemetry_refinements.steady_state_cost: Measure decode-only time excluding first prefill

success_criteria.crossover_identified: required — find the decode length where B011 < B010 in wall time
success_criteria.or_no_crossover: acceptable — if no crossover found, report that and explain why
success_criteria.numerical_equivalence: PASS required at each decode length
success_criteria.telemetry_captured: All metrics_per_run captured for both B010 and B011

b012_test_harness.description: Create test harness that runs varying decode lengths with/without cache

b012_crossover_analysis.description: Analyze results to find crossover point

notes: B012 tests the amortization hypothesis from B011
The statement that cache becomes faster for 100+ tokens is currently a hypothesis, not measured
B012 must separate cache population cost from steady-state residency cost
If no crossover is found, that is a valid result — report it honestly
